canonical_name: XLand-MiniGrid -- XLand-MiniGrid: Scalable Meta-Reinforcement Learning Environments in JAX (Alexander Nikulin, Vladislav Kurenkov, Ilya Zisman, Viacheslav Sinii, Artem Agarkov, Sergey Kolesnikov; NOT_FOUND_AT_PIN (GitHub org 'corl-team'; institution not stated in tree); 2023-2025)
lineage: README: 'inspired by the diversity and depth of XLand and the simplicity and minimalism of MiniGrid'; 'comes with example environments ported from the original MiniGrid'; benchmarks 'following the procedure used to train DeepMind AdA agent from the original XLand'; baselines 'in the PureJaxRL style'; API 'combines dm_env and gymnax interfaces' after trying Jumanji; See Also lists Brax, Gymnax, Jumanji, Pgx, JaxMARL, Craftax, Purejaxql. Commented-out README note references XLand-100B dataset (github.com/dunno-lab/xland-minigrid-datasets) 'based on XLand-MiniGrid'. || main loop (reader, from the code): Environment.step applies the agent's action to the grid (take_action), then lax.scan's over the task's encoded production rules (check_rule, lax.switch dispatch per rule) to transform grid/agent, then evaluates the encoded goal (check_goal) to decide termination and a time-discounted reward of 1 - 0.9*step/max_steps, truncating at max_steps; the meta-training loop (train_meta_task.make_train) samples a fresh batch of rulesets from a Benchmark each meta-update and runs recurrent PPO over multi-trial rollouts.

entry_points: src/xminigrid/environment.py Environment (abstract base; reset() calls _generate_problem then builds a TimeStep; step() applies take_action, then check_rule over the rule encodings, then check_goal for termination, reward = 1 - 0.9*(step_num/max_steps) on success, truncation at max_steps)

src/xminigrid/envs/xland.py XLandMiniGrid (the meta-RL environment: default_params sets view_size=5 and max_steps=3*H*W; _generate_problem picks a room layout R1/R2/R4/R6/R9, places ruleset.init_tiles at random coordinates and the agent, and stores goal_encoding/rule_encoding from the ruleset)

src/xminigrid/core/rules.py check_rule + BaseRule subclasses (jax.lax.scan over rule encodings, jax.lax.switch on encoding[0] to dispatch among 12 rule classes: EmptyRule, AgentHoldRule, AgentNearRule, TileNearRule, TileNear{Up,Right,Down,Left}Rule, AgentNear{Up,Right,Down,Left}Rule; each rule transforms grid/agent when its condition holds)
src/xminigrid/core/goals.py check_goal + BaseGoal subclasses (same dispatch pattern over 15 goal classes; goals only test conditions, never mutate state)

src/xminigrid/benchmarks.py Benchmark / load_benchmark (flax struct holding padded arrays of goals, rules, init_tiles, num_rules; sample_ruleset/get_ruleset/shuffle/split/filter_split; load_benchmark downloads from HuggingFace on first use; registered names trivial-21k, small-1m, medium-1m, medium-3m, high-1m, high-3m)

scripts/ruleset_generator.py sample_ruleset / __main__ (offline, python-random based generator: samples a goal, then a chain of production rules of depth chain_depth whose outputs feed the level above, optional pruning, distractor objects and distractor rules; rejection-samples unique rulesets, pads and saves bz2 pickle)

training/train_meta_task.py make_train / train (pmap'd recurrent PPO meta-training loop: per meta-update vmap benchmark.sample_ruleset over envs, reset, then inner PPO updates over trials with prev_action/prev_reward inputs; logs to wandb, optional orbax checkpoint)
src/xminigrid/registration.py make / register / registered_environments (gym-style registry; src/xminigrid/__init__.py registers XLand-MiniGrid-R{1,2,4,6,9}-NxN and ported MiniGrid-* envs)

example.input: Python snippet in README: benchmark = xminigrid.load_benchmark(name="trivial-21k"); ruleset = benchmark.sample_ruleset(ruleset_key); env, env_params = xminigrid.make("XLand-MiniGrid-R9-25x25"); env_params = env_params.replace(ruleset=ruleset); timestep = jax.jit(env.reset)(env_params, reset_key); timestep = jax.jit(env.step)(env_params, timestep, action=0)
example.output: README: 'timestep is a dataclass containing step_type, reward, discount, observation, as well as the internal environment state'; env.render(env_params, timestep) returns an rgb_array (np.ndarray) or rich_text string per environment.py. Training script prints 'Final return: <float>' and logs eval/returns_mean to wandb. No literal output values given in README.
